metadata.title: Locating Heirs
metadata.author: Hull & Hull LLP
metadata.shortDescription: Ian Hull & Suzana Popovic-Montag discuss the process of locating heirs to an estate.

segments.text: hi and welcome to hullen Hull TV I'm
Dana O'Brien and I'm joined by founding
partner Ian Hull and managing partner
Susanna poit monag at hullen Hall LLP an
Innovative Law Firm that practices
exclusively in aate trust and capacity
litigation here at hullen Hull TV we're
exploring the issues around estate
planning that affect you Ian and Susanna
an executive's duties include locating
all heirs who may be entitled to share
in the estate what's the best place to
start Susanna when we're looking to
locate areas what we're really talking
about is trying to find those
individuals who are beneficiaries of the
estate and easy ones are like for
instance you know to my son but when
you've got an extended family member or
someone who can't be readily a found
then in those cases we normally start
with family and friends to say you know
do you know where these individuals are
can you help us build out this family
tree to find out where everyone is and
that's not necessarily going to lead you
to the right answer many people know and
use the internet they'll do the Canada
411 search they'll do other sort of
self- Health remedies to try to locate
these individuals and when that doesn't
work what about hiring a researcher in
to help out well that's right and those
uh people are available uh readily now
there are sort of two types of
researchers both of which are necessary
and sometimes uh required in different
situations I mean you can hire a fee for
service researcher who has got
genealogical searching that they'll go
right down to going into cemeteries
tracking where family members uh yeah
it's a lot of fun uh and then also
Searchers who will search for a fee and
they will seek you out or you will seek
them and retain them for whatever finder
fee they collect from finding the
individuals now an executive is expected
to make a reasonable effort to find
missing heirs but what's reasonable
Susanna that's a great question and it's
really going to determine or be
determined by the particular situation
so if you uh have gone through the
self-help remedies of trying to locate
individuals you've then hired perhaps a
private investigator or retained one of
these researchers to locate these people
then at that point you may have done
your your reasonable efforts to locate
someone and what happens Ian if an
executive isn't satisfied that they've
found all missing airs what's the next
option well you can uh go to court and
get some assistance from the court and
the steps that suzanna's talked about we
can document them fully and identify
this the self-help remedies that you've
sought identify the researcher and the
researcher will typically file a report
in respect of what efforts they've taken
even that though the court is going to
be very nervous about making an order
and uh lots of times and done these over
the years many times a judge will say
look you know what I'm just not quite
ready to determine uh that you've done
everything because of the consequences
significant uh to this individual if you
determine that they can't be found or
that they can be found so you sometimes
a judge will send you back with a
creative point that they've made and
they'll say well you searched Google but
you didn't search Yahoo and I want you
to go back and do another search uh and
that is not uncommon because of the
consequence of it so might like to give
it a little more time and effort
absolutely Ian and Susanna thank you and
thanks for joining us on Halland Hall
TV
